Assignment 05 / Sculpting for Design

Abstract Wiring

We connected two contrasting wire-and-paper forms into one hanging composition.

Wire · Paper · Positive & negative space

Group project with Sudiksha Suresh and Astha Chand

I worked with Sudiksha Suresh and Astha Chand to plan two connected wire forms. We wanted them to contrast with one another while belonging to one larger composition.

01

Planning a piece together

As three people working together, we wanted to create two pieces that could attach to one another and interact. We explored possible hanging structures before developing an hourglass-like arrangement.

Our sketches record possible outlines, suspension points, and the relationship between the upper and lower forms. We also considered how paper could change the spaces created by the wire framework.

02

Positive and negative

We planned two attached tetrahedral forms. In one, we used paper to fill positive spaces created by the wiring; in the other, we filled negative spaces. This gave the two halves a shared language while keeping them visually distinct.

We used wire to establish the edges and connections, then added butter paper to create translucent surfaces and cut-away shapes. Open gaps allow the surrounding space to remain visible through the sculpture.

03

An hourglass in space

We developed the idea into a hanging, abstract hourglass form. Two tapered sections meet around a narrow connection, with the wider ends extending away from the centre.

We photographed it from three angles to show how the paper surfaces and open gaps change as the piece is viewed from different positions.

04

A proposed home for the work

At the time of our submission, we planned to paint the wires and butter paper and hang the piece in our hostel wing. Our photographs document the construction before that proposed finishing stage.

We brought two differently treated forms together so that they could be read as parts of a single suspended object.
